message.content:
I don’t have a way to see your actual connection from here, so I can’t tell you the exact numbers.  
But you can quickly find out yourself with a few simple steps:

---

## 1️⃣ Use the Speedtest website (recommended)

1. Open a web browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari, etc.).  
2. Go to **[speedtest.net](https://www.speedtest.net)**.  
3. Click the big “Go” button.  
4. Wait a few seconds – the page will display:
   * **Download** speed (Mbps)  
   * **Upload** speed (Mbps)  
   * **Ping** latency (ms)

That’s the most straightforward way to get a real‑time measurement.

---

## 2️⃣ Run a speed test from the command line (Windows)

If you prefer a terminal, you can use the free `speedtest-cli` tool.

### Install `speedtest-cli`

```powershell
# Open PowerShell as Administrator
pip install speedtest-cli
```

> If you don’t have Python or pip installed, you can download the installer from the official Python website first.

### Run the test

```powershell
speedtest
```

You’ll see output similar to:

```
Testing from Your ISP (Your City)...
Retrieving speedtest.net configuration...
Testing download speed........................................
Testing upload speed..........................................
Done!   Download:  45.23 Mbit/s   Upload:  12.34 Mbit/s   Ping:  15.6 ms
```

---

## 3️⃣ Use Windows built‑in tools (quick check)

While not as precise as a dedicated speed test, you can still get a rough idea:

```powershell
# Open PowerShell
Get-NetAdapterStatistics | Select-Object Name, ReceivedBytes, SentBytes
```

This shows raw byte counts; you’d need to calculate throughput over time manually.

---

## 4️⃣ Mobile Apps

If you’re on a phone, apps like **Speedtest by Ookla**, **Fast.com**, or **OpenSignal** give instant results.

---

### Quick recap

| Method | How to run | What you get |
|--------|------------|--------------|
| Browser | Visit speedtest.net | Download/Upload/Ping |
| PowerShell | `speedtest` (after installing) | Same as above |
| Mobile app | Download & run | Same as above |

Pick whichever feels easiest for you. Once you run it, you’ll know exactly what your current internet speed is.
